general.purpose: staq is a quantum compiler and software toolkit for the openQASM language, intended to provide transformation, optimization, and compilation tools over a single common language and target multiple simulation and hardware execution platforms. It also aims to support state-of-the-art circuit transformation algorithms natively on any valid quantum program.

type_evidence.evidence: staq is a new compiler and software toolkit for the openQASM language [15] written in C++.
At this time, staq supports classical logic written in (the combinational subset of)the Verilog hardware description language.
Finally, staq can generate quantum code in a variety of formats that encompass many of the currently available quantum platforms [15, 18, 19, 9, 10, 12].
staq also includes an option to output just the resource counts of a program.

automation_level.evidence: For this reason, the compiler automatically applies a desugaring pass after parsing and semantic checks, andan inlining pass preceding a hardware mapping pass.

evaluation_type.evidence: To assess the performance of staq, we compare it against the well-known software toolkit and compilerQiskit [19].

architecture.design_principles: Full-stack quantum processing toolkit; operates on a single common language; supports state-of-the-art circuit transformation algorithms natively on any valid quantum program; follows a UNIX-style design combining small tools through pipelines; stores and operates directly on QASM syntax trees rather than an intermediate representation.
architecture.technological_foundation: standard C++; C++17 standard; openQASM language; QASM syntax trees (QASM ASTs); Verilog hardware description language; EPFL Logic Synthesis Libraries

algorithms.overall_evidence: The remaining synthesis, optimization, and mapping passes are described in more detail in the follow sections.

algorithms.name: T-count optimization
algorithms.evidence: The main optimization of the staq compiler is an extended implementation of Fang andChen's T -count optimization4 algorithm [27].

algorithms.name: CNOT resynthesis / Gray-synth
algorithms.evidence: For these purposes staq includes an optimization pass - CNOT resynthesis -to reduce the number of cx (i.e. CNOT) gates in a program by performing the CNOT-dihedral algorithmGray-synth of Amy, Azimzadeh, and Mosca [25].

algorithms.name: Steiner mapping algorithm
algorithms.evidence: The Steiner mapping algorithm in staq actually implements a more generalform of re-synthesis, targeting CNOT-dihedral6 circuits by using the Gray-synth CNOT-optimization algo-rithm [25] extended with constrained Gaussian synthesis.

challenges.statement: The scalability of staq's optimization algorithms degrades as the number of qubits increases, and improving this remains future work.
challenges.category_evidence: It remains a focus of future work to improve the scalability ofstaq's optimization algorithms as the number of qubits increases.
challenges.strength_evidence: Similarly, in all but one benchmark circuit with the highest numberof qubits, staq was also signiﬁcantly faster.

challenges.statement: Hardware mapping results are inconsistent, with Qiskit outperforming staq on CNOT counts in most cases under some configurations.
challenges.category_evidence: While the Steiner mappingalgorithm with best-fit initial layout was consistently orders of magnitude faster than Qiskit's defaultmapping algorithm, Qiskit outperformed staq in terms of CNOT counts in the majority of cases.
challenges.strength_evidence: While the Steiner mappingalgorithm with best-fit initial layout was consistently orders of magnitude faster than Qiskit's defaultmapping algorithm, Qiskit outperformed staq in terms of CNOT counts in the majority of cases.
